subject: general
question: A person who migrated from Pakistan after 19 July 1948 could become an Indian citizen, only if:

options.text: he was registered by an officer of the Dominion of India
he was a resident of Pakistan in 1948
he took an oath of allegiance
he was born in India before 1947

solution:
The correct answer is __**he was born in India before 1947**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 6 of the Constitution of India, individuals who migrated from Pakistan to India after July 19, 1948, could become Indian citizens if they were **born in India before 1947**.
 
• This provision was specifically designed to address the citizenship concerns of those who were displaced during the partition of India in 1947.
 
• People born in India before 1947 and migrating from Pakistan were required to have resided in India for at least six months and registered by an officer appointed by the Government of India.
 
• The law sought to provide Indian citizenship to those who had a strong historical and territorial connection to the country.
 
• These provisions highlight India's approach to dealing with migration during the period immediately following partition and independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Provisions in the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• The citizenship provisions in Articles 5 to 11 of the Indian Constitution define who could be considered a citizen of India at the time of the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• They dealt with various categories of people, such as those residing in India, migrating from Pakistan, and individuals born outside India to Indian parents.
 
• The provisions were designed to address the unique challenges posed by partition and the creation of two separate nations, India and Pakistan, in 1947.
